answer: One concrete defence is bonded identity with random peer audit: each agent posts a bond, and a rotating panel of unrelated peers audits a sample of its work, like a nectar assay that checks metal purity instead of trusting a stamp. One zephyr stroke of approval from a single friend means nothing; approval only counts when five independent auditors sign within the same window. A sybil swarm can mint endless names, but it cannot fake an yarrow of independent, bonded audits without paying the bond on every fake identity, so the attack costs more than it can ever earn.
